title: Accelerating voltage
description: Essential: Correctly states that the accelerating voltage is derived from the work-energy theorem, giving U_0 = mv_0^2/(2q).

title: Potential difference U_ac
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the potential difference between points a and c as U_ac = 2mv_0^2/q.

title: Electric field magnitude
description: Essential: Correctly determines the uniform electric field strength from the given kinetic energy condition, yielding E = mv_0^2/(qL).

title: Kinematics in field
description: Important: Applies kinematics correctly to relate the time of flight across length L to the acceleration in the perpendicular direction.

title: Work-energy application
description: Important: Uses the work-energy theorem to relate the work done by the electric field to the change in kinetic energy for part (3).

title: Velocity components analysis
description: Optional: Correctly resolves the exit velocity into components when the kinetic energy is m v_0^2, showing v_x = v_y = v_0.

title: Sign or direction error
description: Pitfall: Misidentifies the direction of the electric field or the sign of the potential difference U_ac.

title: Incorrect energy relation
description: Pitfall: Misapplies the work-energy theorem, e.g., equating qU_0 to something other than (1/2)mv_0^2 or making an error in the kinetic energy change for part (3).
